newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's National Rail put on creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's National Rail put on creditwatch.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard and Poor's said on Wednesday it had placed its A-minus long-term rating of Australia's National Rail Corp Ltd on creditwatch with negative implications following the Australian government's decision to sell its shareholding in the company.

On Sunday, the federal government announced that it planned to sell its 72.3 percent stake in National Rail, which operates interstate freight services, along with its Australian National passenger business as a part of a plan to revive the country's rail system and boost the economy by cutting transport costs.

"After the commonwealth government has sold its shareholding to private interests, Standard and Poor's (S&P) expects the credit rating on National Rail to be strongly influenced by the creditworthiness of the purchaser or purchasers and by the shareholding structure," S&P said in a statement.

Although the federal government owns 72.3 percent of the equity of National Rail it has only 45.3 percent of the voting rights, and requires the agreement of other shareholders, the New South Wales and Victorian governments and legislation in the federal and affected states' parliaments to sell its stake.

"Without a supportive ownership structure, National Rail would probably have a rating in the speculative range," S&P said. "This is due to National Rail's limited operating record, its poor, but improving financial profile and an increasingly competitive environment."
S&P said that given the uncertainties associated with the proposed sale, the agency was unlikely to resolve this creditwatch in the short term.
